title: Session rejected after sign-in or sign-up drops you on a blank sign-in form with no message
where: sign-in / Enlist with the Chapter screen, laptop 1440x900
steps: 1. Create an account (Enlist with the Chapter), or sign in with a correct username and password. 2. The login POST /api/auth/login answers 200, then the first authenticated calls (GET /api/users/33/characters and /campaigns) answer 401. 3. Watch the screen.
expected: If the new session is refused, say so (e.g. 'Your account was created, but signing in failed: try again'; or 'Your session ended, please sign in again'). After sign-up, confirm the account exists.
actual: utils/api.js calls onUnauthorized -> gameStore.logout() on any 401 with a token, so the page silently returns to an empty Chapter Admission form: fields cleared, status region empty, no error. After Create account I could not tell whether the account had been made (it had: signing in later hit the same wall). Console shows only 'Failed to load resource: 401'. NOTE: in this run the 401s come from the testing environment's egress proxy (x-proxy-error: 'upstream auth failed: connection CANDELA_BETA'; it fails any request that carries the app's own Authorization: Bearer header), not from the site. But the silent bounce is the site's: any expired/revoked token mid-use gives the same unexplained jump to an empty form.

title: Google sign-in frame has no accessible name; on the sign-up screen it still says 'Sign in with Google'
where: Chapter Admission and Enlist with the Chapter screens
steps: 1. Open the site signed out. 2. Read the accessibility outline. 3. Click Create an account.
expected: The Google button frame is announced with a name (e.g. title='Sign in with Google'); on the Enlist screen the button reads 'Sign up with Google' (GSI text=signup_with).
actual: Outline shows a bare 'iframe' before the status region on both screens, so a screen reader hears an unnamed frame. On the Enlist with the Chapter screen the button still says 'Sign in with Google' (request has text=signin_with).

title: Dispatch button is below the fold on a 1440x900 laptop, with nothing hinting the dispatch card scrolls
where: Lightkeeper's desk, Roster section, dispatch card (left column), 1440x900 (761 px inner height)
steps: 1. Create a campaign and open the Lightkeeper's desk at 1440x900. 2. Look at the dispatch card in the left column, Template mode.
expected: The Dispatch stamp (the one thing the card is for) is visible, or the column shows a scroll cue.
actual: The card ends at 'Secure the area. Light the Way.'; Dispatch and End Assignment sit at y=766, under the window edge. The whole page does not scroll (html is 761 tall); only the left column scrolls, and only with the wheel over it. No scrollbar or fade shows there is more. Found it by measuring the button. Same for the middle column (circle formation papers run off the bottom).

title: Invite player says 'The player rejoins with a new investigator' on a brand-new campaign
steps: 1. Create a new campaign. 2. Open Invite player under Join Requests.
expected: Wording that fits a first invite, or a note that this is for replacing a fallen investigator (a player in this campaign already).
actual: 'The player rejoins with a new investigator, without waiting for your approval.' With no one in the campaign yet, 'rejoins' reads as if it is the wrong tool, and it is not clear whether I can use it to invite Robert by username instead of handing out the code.

title: Sketch tool is quick to use for an improvised scene map
steps: 1. Notebook > Field Notes > Sketch. 2. Draw a pen line, a box in umber, a red arrow, a text label. 3. Cancel.
actual: All tools and inks worked first time with smooth strokes; every tool and ink has a spoken name; Cancel turns into Discard instead of throwing the drawing away, which is a good guard.

title: No sketch in Private Notes, so the Lightkeeper cannot prepare a map before showing it
where: Notebook, Private Notes and Lightkeeper Resources
steps: 1. Notebook > Private Notes (or Lightkeeper Resources). 2. Look for Sketch or Photo.
expected: A way to draw a scene map privately and reveal it to the table later.
actual: Only Field Notes (visible to everyone) has Sketch and Photo. Private Notes and Lightkeeper Resources have text only.

title: Campaign code is not suggested from the campaign name
steps: 1. Hub > New campaign. 2. Type 'The Saltmere Chapter' as the name.
expected: A suggested code (e.g. saltmere-chapter) that I can accept or change.
actual: Code stays empty with placeholder 'e.g. fairelands-01'; Create stays disabled until I invent one.
